questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The level of education at the university, the location and the different culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go on exchange!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A little difficult. NUS uses a lot of different websites for everything, so do keep track of them and the deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much assistance, unless you seek for help yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Not the best introduction and orientation, but they do host different events you can participate in.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Residences, halls and some other options I think.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is not really any cooking facilities, in Singapore you don't cook. Meal plans are included in some of the campus accommodations - mostly halls, not all residences.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Small rooms, but overall fine. It is worth the small living and cheaper price to live on campus - it is much easier to become a part of the campus social life when you live there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in a hall and found it really nice with the social aspect of it and the meal plan - even though the food is not good...

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit confusing, but they have quite a few courses you can follow. Also found more courses we were able to follow, than offered in the first catalogue. "NUSMODS" is a good website to put a schedule together.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have a few rounds to secure your courses. Don't expect to get all your wished courses necessarily.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can email them for help, they usually answer pretty quick. I did not need to seek other help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get all the courses I wanted at first, but I found some good courses anyway.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't panic if you don't secure the best or all of your courses in the start, you have 2-3 rounds to secure the courses you want. Do apply for more courses than you need and then you can drop some of the courses you don't want later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level in Science was pretty good - at least in my courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was pretty similar to KU, if you go for the courses fitting to the year of your study.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less interactive than UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Immunology 
RNA Biology and Technology 
Introductory Bioinformatics
Discover South Asia

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Immunology was a great course - the lectures had a good flow and professors were good at teaching the material. The course also included some practicals in the laboratory.
RNA Biology and technology I also found interesting, but a bit more on the heavy side (not time wise, but content wise).

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The student fees and visa application fees, but not a lot overall. I travelled quite a bit during the semester, which is the reason for the high personal spending.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat, groceries and alcohol was more expensive than I expected, but food in hawker centers was cheaper than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of activities you could participate in, and campus included gyms, pools and many sports teams to join - all for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of clubs, sports teams and social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the orientation and join a club/team if you want.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Singapore (Gardens by the Bay, Tree top walk, National Museum and so on) and travel! It is easy to travel around Asia from Singapore - especially Malaysia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very different in Singapore - very Chinese and Malaysian, but it is also very strict and well behaved country. So I would say it was fine to adjust to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living in a hall with many local students made it easier, but also joining a sports team is a good way I think.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The very serious approach to uni

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I always felt safe in Singapore!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The application process might be a bit overwhelming, but hold tight everything is much easier when you arrive. 
Join all social events in the start and meet new people - every exchange student is very open and nice.
Enjoy your exchange - time flies.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Write down information along the way - your NUS ID, FIN number, deadlines and so on.
Use NUSMODS to put together your schedule.
Pack a sweater to use in the lecture halls - they use a lot of air-condition!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new experiences, the people and the self-development.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the heat and humidity. I had a room without aircon, which could be pretty hot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange! It is a great experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
